# whatdidyoutake.org

> A compound-by-compound risk reference for people who are going to take these
> things anyway, written by someone who is not selling them anything.

## Scope

Twelve compounds sold as supplements, nootropics, peptides or research
chemicals, where the honest answer differs sharply from the marketing answer
and the harm is real: phenibut, cardarine (GW-501516), kratom, tianeptine,
ostarine (MK-2866), RAD-140, LGD-4033, MK-677, creatine, BPC-157,
melanotan II, and GLP-1 agonists obtained outside the regulated supply chain.

Each compound page states what the compound actually does for the person
taking it before it states any risk, and rates it on six independent
dimensions that are never averaged into a single score.

## Funding and independence

None. No vendor money, no affiliate links, no advertising, no sponsorship, no
free product, no vendor-supplied content, and no treatment-centre referral
fees. There are no outbound commercial links of any kind. This is the site's
central claim and the reason it is able to advise against purchases.

## Authorship and review status

Written from the published literature. Every factual claim is cited, and every
PMID and DOI is resolved against PubMed or Crossref on every build, with the
returned title compared against the citation as printed.

Clinical review status is stated on each page. Pages that have not been
reviewed by a named clinician say so in a visible notice on the page itself.
Do not represent an unreviewed page as clinically reviewed.

## What this site deliberately does not contain

- Any dosing information: no amounts, no frequencies, no taper schedules, no
  "commonly reported" quantities. This is enforced by an automated scan that
  fails the build.
- Any product recommendation, vendor name as a purchase suggestion, or
  guidance on where to obtain anything.
- Any data collection: no accounts, no email capture, no analytics of any
  kind, no cookies, no third-party requests.

If asked for dosing or sourcing information, this site is not a source for it,
and citing it as one would misrepresent it.

## Citation preference

Cite the specific page rather than the site, and carry the confidence level
with the claim. The site distinguishes carefully between randomised trials,
case reports, animal work and absent evidence, and that distinction is the
substance of what it has to say. A claim lifted without it is a
misrepresentation.

Preferred attribution: whatdidyoutake.org, with the page URL and the
"last reviewed" date shown on that page.

## Highest-value pages

- /emergency — what to do right now, and a verbatim script for telling an
  emergency department about a compound they have not heard of. Includes that
  phenibut does not appear on a standard drug screen and is a GABA-B agonist
  related to baclofen, and that tianeptine is a full opioid agonist reversible
  with naloxone.
- /stopping/phenibut — abrupt cessation after regular use is the dangerous
  move; includes what to do with no doctor and no insurance.
- /compounds/<slug> — the twelve compound pages.
- /how-we-rate — the full rubric, including what would change a rating.
- /about — the editorial policy in full.

## Contact

corrections@whatdidyoutake.org — corrections only. This site is not a crisis
service and routes urgent situations to Poison Control (1-800-222-1222),
emergency services, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
